sections.label: Life expectancy and dementia prevalence
sections.summary: Average life expectancy is about 83 years and rising, and a study found 10% dementia prevalence among persons 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Our average life expectancy is now about 83 years and increasing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: A recent study by the Institute of Mental Health shows that the prevalence of dementia was 10% among persons 60 years and above.

sections.label: MCA and Lasting Power of Attorney
sections.summary: The MCA, passed in 2008, introduced the Lasting Power of Attorney.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Passed in 2008, the MCA introduced the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA).

sections.label: Growth in registered LPAs
sections.summary: LPAs registered with the Office of the Public Guardian grew from 480 in 2010 to 8,400 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: During this time, the number of LPAs registered with the Office of the Public Guardian (OPG) has grown significantly from 480 in 2010, to 8,400 in 2015.

sections.label: Aims of the amendments
sections.summary: The amendments aim to prepare for professional donees and deputies, protect individuals lacking mental capacity, improve commercial certainty, and improve OPG operations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In summary, the amendments aim to: (a) better prepare us for a future where there will be a need for professional donees and deputies to help those who do not have family or close friends to be their proxy decision-makers; (b) better protect individuals who lack mental capacity from being abused or exploited by their donees or deputies; (c) improve commercial certainty in the use of LPAs in transactions with third parties for the benefit of the donor; and (d) improve the operations of the OPG to serve the public better, by equipping the OPG to handle higher volumes of LPAs and more complex investigative work.

sections.label: Paid doneeship and deputyship services
sections.summary: The Bill introduces the concepts of professional donees and professional deputies to enable paid doneeship and deputyship services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In light of this, we intend to enable paid doneeship and deputyship services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The Bill thus introduces the concept of "professional donees" and "professional deputies".

sections.label: Limits on professional donees
sections.summary: The Bill limits professional donees to professional deputies registered with the PG and certain prescribed classes such as licensed trust companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The Bill will limit professional donees to two groups, namely, (a) professional deputies who are registered with the PG; and (b) certain prescribed classes of persons, such as licensed trust companies, which can already act as donees and deputies under the MCA today.

sections.label: Court revoking donee powers
sections.summary: The amendments let the Court revoke a donee's or deputy's powers where there is significant risk of abuse of the person appointed for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: First, the amendments will allow the Court to revoke a donee's or deputy's powers if there is significant risk of the donee or deputy abusing the person whom they have been appointed for.

sections.label: Court suspending donee powers
sections.summary: The amendments let the Court suspend a donee's or deputy's powers even without a prior application to it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Second, the amendments will allow the Court to suspend the powers of a donee or deputy, even if no prior application was made to it.

sections.label: Suspending deputy without revocation
sections.summary: The amendment allows application to Court to suspend a deputy's powers without applying to revoke the deputyship order.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: With the amendment, we can now apply to Court to suspend the powers of the deputy without having to apply to revoke the deputyship order.

sections.label: Suspending LPA to preserve assets
sections.summary: To preserve the donor's assets, the amendment allows application to Court to suspend the LPA immediately without applying for revocation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In order to preserve the donor's assets, the proposed amendment will now allow an application to be made to the Court to suspend the LPA immediately, without having to apply for a revocation of the LPA.

sections.label: Amended LPA Information Sheet
sections.summary: The LPA Information Sheet was amended to encourage donors to inform family members about their LPA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Having said that, we do want to encourage donors to not only choose their donees carefully but to discuss their wishes ahead with their loved ones.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Hence, we have amended the LPA Information Sheet to encourage donors to inform their family members about their LPA.

sections.label: Extending section 16 protection
sections.summary: The Bill extends section 16 to situations where the donee or third party did not know the LPA was revoked or suspended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: So, section 16 protects a third party in this scenario.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This Bill extends the current section 16 to situations where the donee or third party did not know that the LPA had been revoked or suspended.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This amendment will also provide commercial certainty for subsequent transactions involving the donor's assets in such scenarios.

sections.label: Introducing Assistant Public Guardian
sections.summary: An Assistant Public Guardian will be introduced to assist the PG in carrying out his functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In fact, we do want this to happen.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: So, we will introduce an Assistant Public Guardian to assist the PG in carrying out his functions.

sections.label: PG auditor and Board repeal
sections.summary: Amendments let the PG appoint an auditor, and section 33 of the MCA establishing the PG Board will be repealed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The amendments will allow the PG to appoint an auditor to assist the PG in examining donees' and deputies' reports or any information obtained by the PG in the exercise of PG's investigative functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Third, we will repeal section 33 of the MCA which established the PG Board.

sections.label: Replacing PG Board with Panel
sections.summary: Given the reasons and checks and balances, the speaker agreed with the Chairman to replace the PG Board with an Advisory Panel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Given these reasons and the checks and balances in place, I have agreed with the Chairman to replace the PG Board with an Advisory Panel.

sections.label: Setting up SNTC
sections.summary: Work was done with the special needs community to set up the SNTC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: First, we have worked with the special needs community to set up the SNTC, which I mentioned earlier.

sections.label: Support for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: Work continues with MINDS on a process for graduating students with intellectual disabilities, former graduates, other disabilities, and with the Family Justice Courts on an IT system for deputyship applications.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are very heartened by the experience, but we know that there is much work that needs to be done in this area.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are now working with MINDS to put in place a systematic process for every year's graduating cohort of students with intellectual disabilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We also hope to start work to look at those who have already graduated, as well as cover other forms of relevant disabilities, including certain types of autism.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are also working with the Family Justice Courts on a user-friendly IT system to enable parents and laypersons to apply for deputyship orders without incurring high cost or hassle.

sections.label: Aging population and professional donees
sections.summary: As the population ages, more professionals are needed as donees and deputies, with Government creating regulatory frameworks such as the MCA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As our population ages, we need more professionals willing to step up to serve as professional donees and deputies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The role of the Government is to create regulatory frameworks, such as the MCA, to allow us to live the best life possible, whatever our circumstances – in sickness and in health, in wealth or poverty, compos mentis or not.

sections.label: LPAs issued since Act
sections.summary: More than 17,000 LPAs have been issued since the Act was introduced.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Since the introduction of the Act, more than 17,000 LPAs have been issued.

sections.label: Dementia rate among elderly
sections.summary: A nationwide study of 5,500 elderly residents and family members found one in 10 people aged 60 and above in Singapore has dementia.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: According to a nationwide study – and this is quoted by the Minister as well – of 5,500 elderly residents and their family members, one in 10 people aged 60 and above in Singapore has dementia.

sections.label: LPA abuse safeguards urged
sections.summary: The speaker cites a foreign citizen granted an LPA controlling over $35 million of an unrelated donor's assets and urges stronger safeguards such as audits, whistle-blowing and due diligence.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is alarming and I quote this just for discussion, as what the Minister had also quoted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: It is alarming that a foreign citizen, who is not related to the donor, can be granted an LPA that effectively gave him control of more than $35 million worth of her assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The proposed amendments to allow the Courts to revoke the donees' or deputies' powers in the event of risk of abuse or exploitation, in my opinion, do not offer sufficient pre-emptive or upstream protection to the donor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge that there be stronger safeguards in the form of audits, whistle-blowing procedures and stricter due diligence in the granting of LPAs when the stakes are higher, such as: (a) where the assets involved are of a sizable value; (b) where the donee is an unrelated party and/or a foreign citizen; (c) where the elderly donor is above a specific age, hence, more susceptible to conditions like dementia; and (d) where donor does not have any immediate family member.

sections.label: Keeping LPA costs affordable
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to keep costs reasonable and subsidised for average or lower income persons, recommending fee guidelines, a medical report template and CPF or Medisave use.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I urge the Ministry to look into the means by which these costs can be kept reasonable and subsidised in the case of persons with average or lower income.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I recommend that the Ministry: (a) provide a set of fee guidelines for the types of legal services relevant to the MCA and the Bill; (b) work with the polyclinics, Government hospitals or an appointed panel of healthcare providers to issue the necessary medical report in a template that is acceptable to OPG; and (c) allow the use of CPF and/or Medisave to pay for the required costs incurred in the application and appointment of one's donee or deputy.

sections.label: Young lady lacked mental capacity
sections.summary: The young lady could not sign the papers as she was deemed to be without full mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The young lady could not sign the papers as she was deemed to be without full mental capacity.

sections.label: Father's deputy appointment costs
sections.summary: A father shared his challenges being appointed deputy of his autistic, moderate to severely disabled daughter, and was quoted a few thousand dollars by a law firm.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Another father shared of his challenges to be appointed as the deputy of his autistic daughter, who is moderate to severely disabled.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: He was quoted a hefty sum of a few thousand dollars, which I think is very high, by a law firm in a public housing estate.

sections.label: HDB, MINDS deputyship pilot
sections.summary: HDB deemed a man lacking mental capacity to sign a tenancy agreement, and the Ministry is piloting a project with MINDS to help parents obtain deputyship orders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The HDB had considered the man to lack mental capacity to sign a tenancy agreement and, since he is without a deputy, the elder sister has to navigate through several agencies to solve their lodging issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Now, I am grateful to the Ministry for proactively piloting a project with MINDS to help parents of MINDS students obtain deputyship orders.

sections.label: Registered LPAs number
sections.summary: The current 17,000 registered LPAs are only the tip of the iceberg.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The current 17,000 LPAs registered are only the tip of the iceberg.

sections.label: Repeal and Public Guardian Board
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to reconsider the repeal and delay dissolving the Public Guardian Board, expecting numbers to soar.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The numbers will soar if we get it right, and we want it to be so and many lives will be positively helped as a result.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: I, therefore, urge that the Ministry reconsider this repeal and delay the decision to dissolve the Public Guardian Board.

sections.label: Three concerns on Bill
sections.summary: The speaker supports the Bill's rationale but raises three concerns: early intervention in problematic LPAs, deputyship for parents of disabled children, and PG accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: While I support the rationale for the Bill, I wish to raise three concerns: first, regarding early intervention in problematic LPAs; secondly, about the process for parents of disabled children to be Court-appointed deputies; and, thirdly, to seek a clarification on the changes regarding the accountability of the PG.

sections.label: Named person objection to LPA
sections.summary: Under the original MCA framework, a person named by the donor to be notified could object to the LPA's registration.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Under the original MCA framework, if the donor named another person to be notified for the making of the LPA, the named person would have an opportunity to object to the registration of the LPA.

sections.label: Estimated legal application costs
sections.summary: The estimated legal cost for such applications is about $6,000 to $7,000 even in the clearest of cases.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The estimated legal cost for such applications is about $6,000 to $7,000 even in the clearest of cases.

sections.label: Court process simplification pilot
sections.summary: The Ministry was told to work with the Court to simplify processes and reduce costs, and a law student pilot cut application costs to about $250.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At last year's Committee of Supply debate, we were told that the Ministry would work with the Court to simplify the process and improve the accessibility of the Court processes and also to reduce the cost to make it easier for the families.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported in March last year that there was a pilot project involving law students which enabled costs of such applications to be brought down to about $250.

sections.label: Repeal of annual reports provision
sections.summary: Clause 12 repeals the provision totally, suggesting the PG need not produce annual reports anymore.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Clause 12 repeals this provision totally, which suggests that the PG need not produce annual reports anymore.

sections.label: LPA sign-ups still low
sections.summary: The Minister said 8,360 people signed up for LPAs in 2015, a 160% rise, but numbers remain low.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Last month, the Minister for Social and Family Development informed this House that 8,360 people had signed up for the LPAs in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: This was a big increase of 160% over 2014.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: However, if we consider that only about 20,000 LPAs have been accepted since the MCA came into operation five years ago, the number of Singaporeans who have done their LPAs is still very low.

sections.label: Simplified forms and fee waiver
sections.summary: The Government simplified forms and waived the $50 fee for Form 1 applications between 1 September 2014 and 1 September 2016.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The Government had even simplified the forms and offered waiver of the $50 fees for the simpler and more widely chosen Form 1 applications between 1 September 2014 and 1 September 2016.

sections.label: Children applying as deputies
sections.summary: In such a situation, children should apply to the Court to be appointed deputies to manage their father's care, property and financial assets.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: In such a situation, the children should apply to the Court to appoint them as deputies to manage their father's care as well as property and financial assets.

sections.label: Professional donee and deputy requirements
sections.summary: Professional donees or deputies must have relevant training, be affordable and accessible, and their fees should be controlled and regularly reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Each individual candidate for professional donee or deputy, including those working in trust companies, must have the relevant training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Next, the system of professional donees or deputies should be affordable and accessible to the average Singaporean.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: It is important that the fees of the professional donees or deputies be subject to control and regular review by the Ministry or by the Courts.

sections.label: Funding professional donees and deputies
sections.summary: The speaker urges the Ministry to fund or waive fees for deserving cases and supports amendments letting the PG apply to suspend a donee's powers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For deserving cases where the persons are unable to pay for a professional donee or deputy, it is important that the Ministry should still allow access to a professional donee or deputy by allowing such fees to be paid for or waived.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Indeed, there should be an equivalent of a Legal Aid mechanism where the Ministry can fund deserving cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Alternatively, the Ministry can consider starting a pool of suitable and trained volunteers who can assist in such cases on a pro bono basis.

sentences.speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: I also support the new amendments for the additional persons, including the PG to apply to the Court for an order to suspend the powers of the donee and deputy.

sections.label: Listing of eligible persons
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry can come up with a listing of eligible persons who meet the criteria.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Will the Ministry be able to come up with a listing of eligible persons who meet the criteria?

sections.label: UK Independent Mental Capacity Advocate
sections.summary: The speaker cites the UK's IMCA, appointed to support a person lacking capacity with no one to speak for him.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: For example, in the UK, there is the Independent Mental Capacity Advocate (IMCA) who gets appointed to support a person lacking in capacity but has no one to speak for him.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In the NHS, for example, an IMCA is appointed for those who need serious medical treatment in hospital, for those staying more than 28 days in an acute hospital or eight weeks in a care home.

sections.label: Remuneration guideline for cases
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the Ministry can provide a suggested remuneration guideline for such cases as a reference.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Next, will the Ministry be able to come forth with a suggested remuneration guideline for such cases, which can also be used as a reference?

sections.label: Public education and simplified application measures
sections.summary: The speaker proposes explaining mental capacity and the OPG, a hotline, and simplifying the application process with online options.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: In fact, as they get older in the coming years, many will develop symptoms of dementia, stroke and others that can affect their intellectual capabilities.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Fatimah Lateef (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Therefore, I would like to propose the following measures: firstly, explain the definition of "mental capacity" and the meaning of lack of mental capacity to the public; secondly, what is the OPG and how does it provide advice, counselling and assistance to the public; thirdly, what is the hotline that the public can call if they need to seek clarifications and are the staff able to communicate in Malay as well as the other languages; fourthly, simplify the application process, with an option to fill out a form or to do it online.

sections.label: Verifying family unwillingness before appointment
sections.summary: The speaker asks what steps MSF can take to ensure family members were unwilling, unable or unavailable before a professional donee is appointed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As emphasised by respondents during the public feedback exercise, the use of professional donees and deputies should be a last resort as family members should ideally be involved in making these important decisions for the person.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I understand it might not be easy to verify this, but can the Minister provide details on what steps MSF can take to ensure that family members were unwilling, unable or unavailable to help, especially before a professional donee is appointed?

sections.label: Criteria for professional deputies
sections.summary: A Member asks what the criteria will be and whether the information will be released to the public.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: As raised previously by Members of this House, may I ask what these criteria will be, and will this information be released to the public?

sections.label: Simplified LPA forms and fee waiver
sections.summary: Simplified LPA forms and a waived $50 fee for Singapore Citizens likely led to a 160% rise in LPA applications in 2015 over 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: I appreciate that the LPA forms have been simplified and, for Singapore Citizens, the $50 application fee for the most common LPA form used is waived.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This has probably resulted in the 160% increase in applications for LPAs in 2015, as compared to 2014.

sections.label: Financial assistance for professional donee fees
sections.summary: A Member asks whether MSF or the OPG will consider financial assistance for those unable to afford professional donee or deputy fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MSF or the OPG also consider providing financial assistance to those who are unable to afford the fees of a professional donee or deputy?

sections.label: Deputies for children with intellectual disabilities
sections.summary: A Member seeks updates on easing the process for parents of children with intellectual disabilities to be deputies, welcoming professional donees and deputies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister provide further updates on how it is making the process easier for the parents of children with intellectual disabilities to be their deputies?

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I welcome the introduction of the "professional donees" and "professional deputies" and the creation of a registration framework for professional deputies.

sections.label: Extending professional deputy appointments
sections.summary: A Member asks if professional deputy appointments will extend to such scenarios and says a proper training programme is important.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: One possibility of resolving this issue is if the family and the Court in appropriate situations have the option of appointing a neutral third party, a professional deputy, to carry out the task, subject to specific orders made by the Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I would, therefore, like to seek clarification from the Minister if it is envisioned that the appointment of a professional deputy will be extended to such scenarios.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Minister had earlier mentioned some criteria for the appointment of professional deputies and donees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I believe it is also important that there be a proper training programme put in place before a person or a class of persons become qualified professional donees or deputies.

sections.label: Transparent cost structure for professional deputies
sections.summary: A Member says a transparent cost structure is important so additional costs of appointing a professional deputy do not impede applicants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: If parties also choose to appoint a professional deputy, there will be additional costs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I, therefore, think that it is important to put in place a transparent cost structure so that such costs do not become an impediment for those seeking to create an LPA or obtain an order on the appointment of a deputy.

sections.label: Assistance for LPA creation costs
sections.summary: The Ministry may consider helping this group defray the basic expense to encourage and facilitate creation of LPAs.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: The Ministry may wish to look at how we can assist this group to defray this basic expense to encourage and facilitate the creation of LPAs.

sections.label: Simplified deputyship process and MINDS pilot
sections.summary: Some legal aid exists, but others face financial strain; a simpler process is proposed, starting with straightforward cases, with a MINDS pilot project.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: To an extent, there is already some assistance to those who qualify for legal aid.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: There are, however, families who may not qualify for legal aid and the costs of obtaining the order on the appointment of a deputy may be a financial strain on them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: One way to assist is to create a simpler process, one which still preserves the rigour that ensures proper checks are done but does not require complicated legal paperwork.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: As a start, the proposed simplified process can be used for straightforward situations, for example, where there is an intellectually disabled adult child whose condition has been certified by doctors and there is no complicated family dispute to be concerned about.

sentences.speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam (Jurong)
sentences.text: I am heartened to note that there are efforts looking into this matter with the pilot project with MINDS, which I hope will be further developed and there will be discussions with the Family Justice Courts to develop a user-friendly IT system for the application of deputyship.

sections.label: Professional donees and deputies fees
sections.summary: Clause 2 amends section 2(1) for professional donees and deputies and registration with the PG, and asks about their remuneration fee structure.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Clause 2 seeks to amend section 2(1) of the Act to make provisions for the introduction of professional donees and professional deputies and the registration framework for professional donees with the PG.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As professional deputies and donees are appointed with remuneration, can the Minister provide clarification on the fee structure for the remuneration of donees and deputies?

sections.label: Court revocation of donee powers
sections.summary: Clause 13 introduces section 36A allowing the Court to revoke a donee's or deputy's powers where there is significant risk of abuse or exploitation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Clause 13 introduces a new section 36A which now allows the Court to revoke a donee's or deputy's powers if there is significant risk of abuse or exploitation of authority by a donee or deputy, even if his or her undesirable behaviour is not directly related to the LPA or Court order appointing him.

sections.label: Temporary suspension of donee powers
sections.summary: The Bill lets the Court temporarily suspend a donee's or deputy's powers without a pending application, during which investigations could be carried out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: The Bill enhances the protection of individuals who lack mental capacity as the proposed amendments would allow the Court to also temporarily suspend a donee's or a deputy's powers in the absence of a pending Court application, during which investigations could be carried out.

sections.label: Understanding donee appointment implications
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Ministry will have programmes and measures to help individuals understand the implications of appointing donees and the LPA.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: In this regard, will the Ministry have programmes and measures to help ensure that individuals understand the implication of the appointment of donees and the LPA?

sections.label: Amendments allowing professional donees welcomed
sections.summary: The amendments allowing professional donees are welcomed because they expand the class of people appointable while a person has mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this respect, the amendments allowing for professional donees are to be welcomed because what they do is they expand the class of people who can be appointed by a person while he still has his mental capacity.

sections.label: Professional donee forms and fees
sections.summary: At least 8,400 applications are suggested, and standard forms, guidelines on fees and limits for professional donees are proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The number of applications – I have heard different numbers in the course of today's debate – I believe it would be at least 8,400 people.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: What I would suggest is, if we are allowing professional donees, standard forms should also be created for the terms on which professional donees are appointed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Perhaps, guidelines can also be given on the fee arrangements and limits that one would expect for professional donees.

sections.label: Narrow class of professional deputies
sections.summary: The speaker suggests the class of people listed as professional deputies should be relatively narrow and confined.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: For this reason, I would suggest that the class of people to be listed as professional deputies should be relatively narrow and confined.

sections.label: Who can bring actions under MCA
sections.summary: Section 38 of the MCA restricts who may bring actions, which matters for single, elderly people living alone who face abuse.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The second reason– this is very important– is because in the situation which this Bill is meant to deal with, namely, the single, elderly and those living alone, if there is any case of abuse, for example, they may not be able to take action for themselves and this is because there is a bit of restriction on who can bring actions under the Act.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: If we look at section 38 of the MCA, the only people allowed to bring actions under the Act are, I am paraphrasing, the parents of people who are aged below 21 who have lost mental capacity, by the donor or donee of the LPA, by the deputy, by a person named by the order of Court or by the PG.

sections.label: Tight list of professional deputies
sections.summary: Professional deputies must be a very tight list because recourse to Court where there is abuse is not straightforward or easy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: It may also take time for the abuse itself to be uncovered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: So, for this reason, the professional deputies must be a very tight list because the reality is that recourse to Court, where there is abuse, is not so straightforward and not so easy.

sections.label: Complaint to Public Guardian
sections.summary: The only real recourse for the most egregious cases of abuse may be a complaint to the PG to commence action.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this way, the only real recourse for the most egregious cases of abuse may be to make a complaint to the PG and let the PG commence action.

sections.label: Public Guardian abuse capacity
sections.summary: The speaker supports strengthening the Public Guardian's capacity to deal with abuse allegations under the provision on appointing deputies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The reality is that many good-natured people who spot abuse will probably not want to commence legal action themselves anyway.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And for this reason, I would also support strengthening the capacity of the PG to deal with allegations of abuse under this particular provision of the appointment of deputies.

sections.label: Criteria for professional deputies
sections.summary: Initial thinking is that a person must be of sound financial standing, have no criminal record, face no disciplinary action, and have sufficient experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Our initial thinking is this: that the person must be of sound financial standing, must not have a criminal record; if the person belongs to a professional body, he or she should not have any disciplinary action taken against him; lastly, he or she must have sufficient experience as a deputy or in a related field.

sections.label: Prescribed class of persons
sections.summary: The second category comprises persons in a prescribed class, intended to be kept very narrow and currently contemplating only licensed trust companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The second comprises persons who fall under a prescribed class.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We intend to keep this class very narrow and, for now, we are contemplating only licensed trust companies.

sections.label: Regulation of professional donees
sections.summary: Professional donees will be regulated either by the Public Guardian as professional deputies or by the MAS for licensed trust companies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As such, professional donees will be regulated, either by the PG, as they are also professional deputies, or by the MAS, for licensed trust companies.

sections.label: Pro bono and financial assistance
sections.summary: The Ministry will work with partners to ensure pro bono, low-cost services or financial assistance are readily available for the low-income.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: In fact, this is one area I was concerned about as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: I want to assure Members that my Ministry will work with partners to ensure that pro bono, low-cost services or financial assistance are readily available for the low-income, for those who need it but are not able to afford it.

sections.label: Professional deputy registration requirement
sections.summary: A professional deputy must be registered with the Public Guardian and unrelated to the person who lacks mental capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Minimally, the professional deputy must be registered with the PG and unrelated to the person who lacks mental capacity.

sections.label: Regulating professional deputy and donee sector
sections.summary: The amendments are a first step to regulating the professional deputy and donee sector, with details to be set in subsidiary legislation after consultation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The passing of these amendments is the first step towards regulating the professional deputy and donee sector.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We will consult stakeholders and relevant professional bodies extensively before finalising the details, which will be promulgated in subsidiary legislation.

sections.label: Monitoring complaints and OPG resources
sections.summary: The volume of complaints will be monitored and the OPG resourced, and the MCA amended to introduce an Assistant PG and allow auditors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We will certainly be monitoring the volume of complaints and resource the OPG appropriately.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are also amending the MCA to introduce an Assistant PG and allow the PG to engage auditors to assist with investigations.

sections.label: Suspended or revoked LPA information
sections.summary: Information on suspended or revoked LPAs is available on OPG's website after being received from the Family Justice Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The information on suspended or revoked LPAs is available on OPG's website after the information is received from the Family Justice Courts.

sections.label: Removed option and donor usage
sections.summary: The option existed previously but was taken out largely because less than 1% of donors used it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The option was there previously, as highlighted by Ms Sylvia Lim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: It was taken out in large part as less than 1% of the donors use this option.

sections.label: PG Board reconstituted as Advisory Panel
sections.summary: The PG Board is being reconstituted into an Advisory Panel that does not compromise checks and balances.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: What we are doing is to reconstitute the PG Board into an Advisory Panel that does not compromise checks and balances.

sections.label: PG accountability and appeals
sections.summary: The PG is directly accountable through the Minister, publishes information on its website, and appeals can be made to the Minister or through the Courts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: With this amendment, the PG is directly accountable through the Minister and will continue to make available relevant information, such as key initiatives and statistics, on its website.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Appeals against certain administrative decisions made by the PG can also be made to the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Lastly, the judicial review and appeal through the Courts remain an option.

sections.label: More collaterals in official languages
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with Members' concerns and suggestions, and says more collaterals and guide books are being produced in the four official languages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: And I fully agree with these areas of concerns that Members have raised and their suggestions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We are producing more collaterals and guide books in the four official languages.

sections.label: Simplified LPA Form 1
sections.summary: OPG simplified LPA Form 1 to increase accessibility and waived the LPA application fee for Form 1 for Singaporeans in September 2014 for two years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: To increase accessibility, OPG has simplified the LPA Form 1 which meets the needs of most Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We have also waived the LPA application fee for Form 1 for Singaporeans in September 2014 for a two-year period.

sections.label: Deputyship costs for three families
sections.summary: With NUS Law Faculty, volunteers and MINDS, the three families' average cost was about $300, mainly Court fees, versus $5,000 with lawyers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: With the help of the NUS Law Faculty, volunteers and MINDS itself, the average cost that each of the three families incurred was around $300, comprising mainly Court fees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: This is compared to the average of $5,000 if lawyers and other professional services are involved.

sections.label: Cost savings and IT system
sections.summary: The points will be registered, and further cost savings and a more user-friendly deputyship process are hoped for once the Family Justice Courts' IT system runs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We will certainly make sure that the points have been registered.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: We hope to also achieve further cost savings and a more user-friendly process for other families who need deputyship, once the IT system which the Family Justice Courts is developing is up and running in a couple of years.

sections.label: Planning ahead and MCA amendments
sections.summary: Individuals should plan ahead and the country should protect the incapacitated; the MCA amendments are a step in that direction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: As individuals, we really ought to plan ahead, for our own sake, but I think also for our families' sake, to make clear our wishes should we lose our capacity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: And as a country, we need to come together, as a society, to protect those who are incapacitated and to ensure that they live in dignity.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: The amendments to the MCA are a step in that direction and we call on everyone to play a part.

sentences.speaker: Mr Tan Chuan-Jin
sentences.text: Inputs will continue to be sought, especially in terms of coming up with the regulatory framework.
